title: VIP Feature Request Budgeting & Runway Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Sales and Customer Success frequently surface high-priority feature asks from top accounts without a clear, deterministic way for Product and Eng to accept, budget, or commit. This results in ad-hoc scope promises, missed commitments, and confusion across GTM and delivery teams.

Goal: Define a lightweight, repeatable protocol that: (1) gates VIP feature requests with a budgeted engineering runway tied to contract class and impact; (2) provides transparent commit windows and rollback rules; (3) automates signals into the roadmap and SLAs for follow-through. The protocol should preserve fairness across accounts and reduce unplanned work that destabilizes roadmap commitments.
background: Context: Redwood has a suite of enterprise and high-touch customers with varying SLAs and revenue contribution. Current intake flows (support tickets, CSM requests, executive asks) lack clear economic guardrails. PMs currently resort to ad-hoc escalations or special sprints. Stakeholders: Sales (quota retention), CSM (renewals), Legal/Contracts, Engineering (capacity), Finance (revenue attribution).
proposed_workflow: Eligibility check: Request must be submitted via the VIP Intake form (CSM or AE) with required fields: customer ARR band, contractual commitments, intended go-to-production date, and business outcome metrics.

Initial triage (24-72h): PM team validates scope and classifies request into one of three buckets: Advisory (no engineering effort), Small deltas (<= 5 dev-days), Sprintable (<= 40 dev-days) or Major (requires roadmap slot).

Budget assignment: Each ARR band maps to a discretionary runway budget (in dev-days/points) per rolling 90-day window. Example mapping: Bronze (<$100k) = 0, Silver ($100k-$1m) = 5 points, Gold ($1m-$5m) = 15 points, Platinum (>$5m) = 40 points.

Commit window & scope-lock: If a request fits the assigned runway budget and Stakeholder Approval is granted, Product issues a 'scope-lock' and schedules work into the next sprint cycle. Scope-lock is limited to a 30-day active development window; beyond that the request is re-evaluated.

Escalation ladder: For scope beyond assigned budget or requiring SLA changes, escalate to Director PM + ENG Manager + CSM Director. Executive priority requests must include written sponsor approval and optional commercial offset (credit or committed contract amendment).
Automatic feedback: Console automation adds a VIP flag to the roadmap item and notifies Sales/CSM via Slack and a linear ticket comment. Metrics and timelines are surfaced on the VIP dashboard.
Outcomes & refunding: If engineering slippage causes a missed committed delivery, CSM triggers a compensation playbook (service credits, extended trial, or contractual remedy) based on severity tier.
Fairness audit: Monthly review of VIP runway usage to detect skewed allocation and adjust mappings or require commercial offset for repeat heavy users.
acceptance_criteria: VIP intake form live and linked in CSM playbook.
Runway budget table published (Finance + Eng agreed formula).
Automation: VIP flag set on Linear ticket and roadmap item within 24h of intake submission.
Dashboards show: count of VIP requests, runway consumed by customer band, time-to-commit, and on-time delivery rate.
Stakeholder sign-off from Sales Lead (Marissa K.), CSM Head (Lena Cho), and Eng Ops (Owen Bryant).
decision_log: 2026-03-10 Aisha P.: Drafted protocol and requested initial stakeholder sync.
2026-03-11 Marco R.: Proposed ARR -> dev-point mapping; suggested 90-day rolling window instead of calendar quarter.
2026-03-12 Lena C.: Requested explicit refund/remedy tiers for missed commitments; added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-12 Owen B.: Engineering requested guardrails around 'scope-lock' to avoid mid-sprint changes.
metrics: Time-to-commit: target <= 21 days for sprintable items
Runway utilization: percent of allotted dev-days consumed by band per 90-day window
On-time delivery rate for VIP items: target >= 90%
Customer satisfaction delta (pre/post delivery) for VIP items
runbook_triggers: VIP intake submitted -> create Linear ticket with label 'vip' and ping PM rotation
Runway budget exhausted for band -> auto-alert Finance and PM Lead, require commercial approval for new work
Missed delivery beyond SLA -> automatically create compensation task in CSM queue
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High-ARR customers monopolize runway -> Mitigation: monthly fairness audit and commercial offset requirement for heavy usage.
Risk: Ambiguous scope leads to mid-sprint churn -> Mitigation: enforce definition-of-done in intake; scope-lock includes explicit acceptance criteria.
Risk: Manual tagging misses requests -> Mitigation: automation via intake form and webhook into Linear/GitHub.
next_steps: Finalize ARR -> dev-point mapping with Finance by 2026-03-18
Build VIP intake form and publish to CSM playbook by 2026-03-22
Implement Linear automation (PR #1823) and test end-to-end by 2026-03-29
Run a 30-day pilot with 3 accounts (one per ARR band) starting 2026-04-01
